Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Emily Carter, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Thompson, Chief Operating Officer; and Lisa Chen, VP of Exploration.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Emily, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy delivered solid results in Q3 2024, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved record production levels and significant strides in capital efficiency amid WTI averaging $82 per barrel. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on ESG initiatives, where we've made meaningful advances in emissions reductions. We're focused on high-return drilling in our core basins, advancing key exploration efforts, and maintaining discipline on capital allocation. Further, we're optimizing our portfolio for sustained free cash flow generation. Finally, we're positioning for long-term growth while navigating market volatility.

To dive deeper into our ESG momentum, I'll turn it over to Sarah Jenkins, our Chief Sustainability Officer.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report strong momentum on our ESG agenda, particularly in advancing our emissions reduction targets, which remain a cornerstone of our strategy to deliver long-term value in a transitioning energy landscape. As you know, we've committed to net-zero Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions by 2035 for our operated assets, with full Scope 1, 2, and 3 net zero by 2050—aligning with the Paris Agreement and ahead of many peers like ExxonMobil and Chevron.

Let me start with the numbers. In Q3 2024, our total Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions stood at 12.4 million metric tons of CO2 equivalent, reflecting an 18% year-over-year reduction from 15.1 million MT in Q3 2023. This puts us 22% ahead of our 2025 interim target of a 15-20% reduction from our 2020 baseline of 18.5 million MT annually. On an intensity basis—key for benchmarking in our industry—our Scope 1+2 emissions per boe of production dropped to 18 kg CO2e/boe, down from 22 kg last year and 25 kg in 2020. That's competitive with leaders like Occidental Petroleum's 17 kg/boe and well below the global upstream average of 28 kg/boe per IEA data.

Methane remains our highest-priority short-term lever, given its potent GWP. We've slashed methane emissions intensity by 28% YoY to 0.25% of gross gas production—on track for our OGCI-aligned goal of under 0.20% by 2025. This was driven by our comprehensive LDAR program: over 60,000 component-level surveys conducted this year using drones and OGI cameras from FLIR and Pergam, identifying and repairing 4,200 high-emission sources. In the Permian Basin, where we operate 1.2 million net acres, we've deployed continuous monitors from Project Canary at 85% of our 450 key pads, achieving 95% uptime and reducing fugitive emissions by 35% in that basin alone.

Flaring is another success story. Routine flaring volumes fell 42% YoY to 0.8% of gross gas, with absolute flared volumes at 1.2 bcf—putting us on pace for zero routine flaring across our portfolio by 2026, two years ahead of our commitment and the World Bank's global initiative. In the Eagle Ford, we've routed 98% of associated gas to sales via our new $150 million midstream JV with Energy Transfer, capturing an incremental 15,000 boe/d while avoiding 250,000 MT CO2e annually.

Regionally, performance varies but trends positively. In the US Lower 48—65% of our production—emissions intensity is now 15 kg CO2e/boe, bolstered by electrification: we've swapped out 1,200 diesel engines for grid-powered electric frac fleets from Halliburton, cutting diesel use by 40% or 180,000 gallons per frac job. North Sea assets, under stricter Norwegian Petroleum Directorate regs, saw a 25% drop to 12 kg/boe, thanks to our $300 million Troll Phase 3 electrification project tying into shore power by Q4 2025. In the Middle East, our ADNOC JV in Abu Dhabi achieved 0.15% methane intensity via AI-driven leak detection from Baker Hughes' Jewel suite, positioning us ahead of regional peers amid rising scrutiny from the UAE's net-zero pledge.

Technically, we're leaning into CCUS at scale. Our Polaris CCUS hub in the Permian—modeled after Occidental's Stratos project—has injected 1.2 million MT CO2 YTD from our own operations and third-party sources like Chevron's nearby fields. Total capex this year hit $450 million across four projects, with tax credits under 45Q yielding $85/ton incentives. We're also pioneering blue hydrogen: our $200 million pilot at the Haynesville ties steam methane reforming with 95% CCS, producing 50,000 tons of H2 annually for export, de-risking future monetization.

Strategically, these efforts aren't just compliance—they're value creators. Our carbon intensity edge has unlocked $2.5 billion in ESG-linked financing this year, including a green bond from BlackRock with a 25 bps pricing kicker for hitting targets. Amid EU CBAM tariffs looming in 2026 and California's Low Carbon Fuel Standard premiums, low-emission barrels command $5-10/boe uplifts in offtake contracts. Peers trading at 8-10x EV/EBITDA multiples versus our 12x reflect this premium—investors like Engine No. 1 and activist funds are rewarding transition leaders.

Looking ahead, Q4 guidance calls for another 5% emissions cut, with $600 million allocated to ESG capex in 2025, ramping CCUS to 5 million MT capacity. Risks like supply chain delays on electrolyzers persist, but our supplier diversification with Siemens and Plug Power mitigates that. We're on a glide path to outperform, ensuring Apex Energy remains a low-cost, low-carbon growth engine.

With that, I'll hand it back to Alex.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, for that comprehensive update. Now, I'll turn the call over to John Ramirez to discuss our financial results in more detail.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $2.1 billion, up 25% year-over-year. Operating income was $1.1 billion, and net income was $850 million. We generated $750 million in free cash flow and returned $350 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $4.8 billion in debt and $1.8 billion in cash.

Good afternoon, everyone. I'll now turn to our financial results, starting with adjusted EBITDA, which came in at $2.8 billion for the quarter – that's a robust 28% increase year-over-year from $2.2 billion in Q3 last year. On a full-year trailing twelve months basis, we're now at $10.7 billion, up 32% from the prior period. This outperformance reflects the strength of our upstream portfolio, disciplined cost management, and favorable macro tailwinds in a volatile commodity environment. Let me break down the key drivers for you.

First, realized pricing was the largest contributor, adding approximately $450 million to EBITDA growth. Our blended realized price per boe averaged $72.50 this quarter, up 22% from $59.40 in Q3 2023. On the crude side, our WTI-linked realizations hit $71.80 per barrel, benefiting from a $4.50/bbl improvement in our Permian differentials versus last year, thanks to expanded takeaway capacity via the Matterhorn Express Pipeline and EPIC Crude Oil Pipeline commitments. Natural gas realizations climbed to $3.25 per Mcfe, a 15% YoY lift, driven by Henry Hub spot prices averaging $2.90/MMBtu amid stronger LNG export demand and lower associated gas flaring penalties in the Permian. We realized about 60% of our oil production hedged at a weighted average floor of $68/bbl, which provided a $120 million tailwind compared to unhedged peers exposed to intra-quarter WTI volatility from $77 to $69.

Production volumes were the second major driver, contributing $380 million to the YoY uplift. Total equivalent production averaged 285 Mbopd, up 14% from 250 Mbopd last year – our highest quarterly rate in company history. Upstream drove this, with oil volumes up 18% to 210 Mbopd. The Permian Basin was the star here, accounting for 62% of our oil output at 130 Mbopd, up 25% YoY on the back of 45 new horizontal wells brought online. We're now running 12 rigs in the Delaware and Midland sub-basins, focusing on 12,000-foot laterals in the Wolfcamp A and B benches with proppant intensities exceeding 2,500 lbs/ft – yielding average 30-day IPs of 1,800 bo/d per well, 20% above our type curve. Cube-style developments, stacking 48 wells per pad, have compressed drill-to-first-oil cycles to under 200 days, boosting capital efficiency.

Regionally, the Eagle Ford added 12% volume growth to 35 Mbopd, leveraging our condensate-rich Eagle Ford Shale assets with enhanced fracture designs incorporating dissolvable diverters, which improved EURs by 15% per well. Offshore Gulf of Mexico contributed steadily at 25 Mbopd from our Lucius and Stones tie-backs, with no hurricane disruptions this year despite Beryl's path nearby. Internationally, our Angola Block 17 volumes held flat at 15 Mbopd, but lower LOE from FPSO optimizations offset Brent discounts. Notably, we divested non-core Bakken assets for $450 million earlier this year, recycling proceeds into higher-margin Permian inventory – a move that's already accretive by 200 bps to our full-cycle FCF yield.

On the cost side, we delivered $250 million in savings, keeping lifting costs at $8.20/boe, down 12% YoY. Lease operating expenses (LOE) per boe fell to $6.50 from $7.80, driven by centralized water management in the Permian – we're now recycling 85% of produced water via our dedicated disposal wells and partnerships with WaterBridge. G&A expenses dropped 8% to $1.10/boe through workforce optimization and AI-powered predictive maintenance, reducing unplanned downtime by 25% across our 1,200-well fleet. DD&A held steady at $14.50/boe, reflecting our emphasis on low-decline assets with PDPs representing 65% of reserves.

Strategic tailwinds rounded out the picture. Refining and marketing margins supported our midstream segment, with 3-2-1 crack spreads averaging $28/bbl versus $22 last year, generating $80 million in EBITDA from our 150 Mbpd Gulf Coast complex – akin to peers like Valero but with lower complexity premiums. No impairments this quarter, unlike ExxonMobil's $1 billion Upstream writedowns earlier this year on Guyana startup delays. Our ESG initiatives, including methane leak detection via FLIR drones, kept flaring below 1% and positioned us favorably for carbon credit monetization under the IRA's 45Q provisions.

Looking ahead, we see sustained momentum into Q4 with Permian activity ramping to 14 rigs and first production from our $300 million Bolt-on acquisition in the Midland Basin, mirroring Occidental's CrownRock synergies. Risks remain around OPEC+ adherence – prolonged cuts could lift Brent to $85 by year-end – but our 55% hedged book and $4.5 billion liquidity shield us. Overall, this EBITDA beat underscores our shift to a high-margin, inventory-rich operator in Tier 1 basins.

Before we open it up to Q&A, I'd like to provide our forward-looking production guidance for Q4 2024 and the full year 2025, along with the key factors shaping these projections. As you know, our strategy remains focused on high-return inventory in the Permian Basin, complemented by selective investments in the Eagle Ford and Gulf of Mexico deepwater assets.

For Q4 2024, we are guiding to 440 to 460 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day (Mboe/d), representing a 5-10% sequential increase from our Q3 actuals of 420 Mboe/d. Oil volumes are expected at 280-295 Mbbl/d (64% of total), NGLs at 70-75 Mbbl/d, and natural gas at 540-580 MMcf/d. This puts us on track for a full-year 2024 average of 425-435 Mboe/d, up 8% from 2023's 393 Mboe/d.

Looking further out to full-year 2025, we're projecting 455-475 Mboe/d, a 7-12% growth trajectory, with oil holding steady at 62-65% of mix. Quarter-by-quarter, we anticipate Q1 at 445-465 Mboe/d, building to 470-490 Mboe/d by Q4 as new D&C programs ramp and turnaround activity wraps up.

Let me walk you through the key factors influencing these projections, starting with the upside drivers, then headwinds, and our mitigation strategies.

Drilling and completions momentum in core basins is the primary upside driver – ~70% of growth. Permian Delaware Basin (65% of 2025 production): We're accelerating our 3-mile lateral program here, with 45 drilled gross wells in Q4 alone across 12 multi-well pads in our Waha and Delaware core areas. Initial production (IP) rates on these laterals are outperforming our type curves by 15-20%, averaging 1,800 Boe/d over the first 30 days (IP-30), thanks to optimized proppant loading at 2,500 lbs/ft and diverter tech reducing heel-toe variance. We've secured 12 frac crews running flat-out, supported by our midstream JV partner—similar to Enterprise Products' model—which gives us 95%+ takeaway certainty via dedicated crude and gas lines. This should deliver 25-30 Mboe/d of net adds in Q4, scaling to 40 Mboe/d incrementally in 2025.

Eagle Ford (15% of production): Our oil-rich Karnes Trough window is firing on all cylinders with 18 new wells online in Q3, posting EURs of 900-1,100 Mboe per well—10% above prior vintages due to our pilot of dissolvable frac balls and real-time fiber-optic monitoring for stage-level optimization. We're layering in a modest waterflood EOR pilot on 2023 pads, targeting 5-8% recovery uplift.

Gulf of Mexico deepwater ramp (high-impact, lumpy adds – 10-15 Mboe/d in 2025): The Winterfell FPSO, our tie-back to the Chevron-operated Ballymore hub, hit first oil in late Q3 ahead of schedule. We're forecasting a Q4 ramp to 12 Mboe/d net, reaching plateau of 18 Mboe/d by mid-2025 at low-20s F&D costs. This mirrors successes like Occidental's recent GoM tie-backs. Additional upside from our King's Quay subsea wells, where we've spudded two infills with high-pressure/high-temp (HPHT) completions.

Base decline and turnarounds (offsetting ~40 Mboe/d annually): Natural decline rates sit at 22-25% corporate, typical for our shale-heavy portfolio. We've offset this with 110 gross wells turned-to-sales (WTS) in Q3, keeping LoC at 1.4 years. Q1 2025 will see ~10 Mboe/d downtime from Permian tank battery upgrades and Eagle Ford rig moves, but we're front-loading D&C to mitigate.

Headwinds and risks: Commodity price sensitivity: At $65-70 WTI (our Q4 realized $68.50), we're hedged 55% on oil volumes for 2025 at $72/bbl swaps and 40% on Henry Hub gas at $3.25/MMBtu. A sustained $5/bbl drop could shave 3-5 Mboe/d via deferred D&C, as half our Permian inventory requires $55-60 breakevens.

Service inflation and supply chain: Sand and guar costs are up 8-10% YoY, echoing 2022 pressures, but our term contracts with Liberty Energy cap this at CPI+2%. Rig counts in Permian are steady at 310 per Baker Hughes, but competition for premium crews could pressure cycle times.

Regional and regulatory: Texas takeaway remains tight—Waha gas basis at -$1.50/MMBtu—but our DPAs with Targa and EnLink provide buffers. No major weather disruptions expected post-Hurricane season, unlike Ida's 2021 hit. ESG-wise, our Permian electrification (80% of pads by YE24) positions us ahead of BLM methane regs.

Strategic insights and capital allocation: Capex guidance holds at $1.15-1.25 billion for 2025 (75% D&C), fully funded from FCF at $60+ oil. Returns target 60-80% IRR on new drills, with 4.5 years of Tier 1 inventory (1.2 Bboe). We're prioritizing bolt-ons like our recent $200M Reeves County acquisition, echoing Pioneer-Nexus synergies, while divesting non-core Bakken for $150M to recycle into Permian.

Long-term, amid OPEC+ cuts extending into 2025 and rising LNG demand (e.g., QatarEnergy expansions), our gas-rich Eagle Ford gives optionality for Gulf Coast LNG feeds.

In summary, this guidance reflects disciplined execution in a $65-75 macro, with Permian driving the bus. We're confident in hitting the midpoint, assuming no black swans.

Moving now to our capital expenditure guidance, which remains a cornerstone of our capital discipline and long-term value creation strategy here at Apex Energy Corporation. As you know, we've consistently delivered on our commitments, generating robust free cash flow even in a volatile macro environment, with WTI averaging around $78 per barrel year-to-date and Henry Hub natural gas holding steady above $2.50 per MMBtu amid growing LNG export demand.

For 2024, we're on track to deliver our full-year capex at the midpoint of our initial guidance range—$2.9 billion—reflecting a 5% reduction from 2023 as we optimized our drilling inventory and leaned into operational efficiencies. We achieved this through a combination of longer laterals—averaging 12,000 feet in the Permian—enhanced frac designs with higher proppant intensity at 2,500 pounds per foot, and multi-well pad development, which drove a 15% improvement in our drilling and completion costs per lateral foot, down to $650 in the core of the Delaware Basin.

Looking ahead to 2025, we're guiding capex to $2.6 billion to $2.8 billion, a modest 5-7% reduction from 2024, underscoring our commitment to base case free cash flow breakeven at $55 WTI and $2.25 Henry Hub. This guidance assumes no major M&A and prioritizes high-return, short-cycle inventory to maximize returns on capital employed, or ROCE, targeting 25-30% at current strip prices. Let me break this down by category and region for clarity.

Upstream Development Capex: $2.2-2.3 billion (80-82% of total). The lion's share goes to our flagship Permian Basin assets, which account for 70% of our 2025 program, or roughly $1.8-1.9 billion. We're planning 85-90 operated wells across 15-18 pads in the Northern Delaware and Midland sub-basins, focusing on our 5-year inventory of Tier 1 locations with sub-$40 WTI half-cycle paybacks. Expect average IRRs of 60-75% on these new drills, based on our proprietary type curves showing 1,200-1,400 MBoe EURs per 1-mile lateral, with 65% oil cuts. We've seen D&C costs stabilize post the Pipeline Express and Matterhorn expansions, alleviating the Waha hub discounts that plagued us in 2023—we're now at parity with WTI.

In the Eagle Ford, we're allocating $350-400 million for 20-25 wells, emphasizing our oil-rich Karnes Trough window. Here, we're rolling out our next-gen completion design—inspired by Pioneer Naturals' high-intensity fracs—pushing proppant loads to 3,000 lbs/ft and incorporating diverter tech for 20% uplift in 30-day IPs, targeting 800-1,000 Boe/d. This should deliver 50-65% IRRs and paybacks under 9 months at $75 Brent.

Appalachia gets $150-200 million for 40-50 Marcellus/Utica wells, capitalizing on the LNG wave with our low-pressure gas gathering system yielding F&D costs below $0.50 per Mcfe. We're guiding for 10-15 Bcfe EURs per well, with recycle ratios exceeding 2.5x, and ROIs north of 40% amid East Coast demand growth.

Exploration and Facilities: $300-400 million (12-14%). We'll invest $200 million in appraisal and tie-backs, including two high-impact pilots in the emerging Last Frontier play in Alaska—modeled after ConocoPhillips' Willow success—where early logs suggest 50-foot net pay in the Nanushuk. Facilities spend focuses on electrification and compression upgrades to cut Scope 1 emissions by 20%, aligning with our net-zero by 2050 pathway and unlocking CCUS tax credits under 45Q.

Corporate and Other: $100-150 million (4-5%). This covers base maintenance, digital initiatives like our AI-driven drilling optimization platform—similar to SLB's Delfi—which has already shaved 10% off rig days—and bolt-on acreage grabs at $5,000-7,000 net acres per $100 oil equivalent.

Our 2025 program is laser-focused on inventory quality over quantity: 85% of spend targets locations with >50% IRR at $60 WTI flat, extending our drilling inventory to 10+ years at current pace. We've stress-tested this at $50 WTI, where we'd still generate $800 million in free cash flow, enabling 100% dividend coverage and $500 million in buybacks. Regionally, Permian's infrastructure maturation—thanks to EPIC and Waha expansions—positions us for sustained differentials under $1/bbl, while Eagle Ford benefits from Gulf Coast refining cracks widening to $15/bbl.

On the tech front, we're doubling down on simultaneous operations (SIMOPS) on pads, achieving 3-4 wells spud per rig per year, and integrating fiber-optic sensing for real-time frac monitoring, boosting recovery factors by 5-10%. Internationally, we're monitoring Guyana's Stabroek block (à la Exxon) for potential farm-ins, but domestic focus remains paramount amid OPEC+ cuts supporting Brent at $75-80.

In summary, this disciplined $2.6-2.8 billion plan positions Apex for $1.4-1.6 billion in levered free cash flow at strip, with NPV10 values exceeding $25 billion on our drilled portfolio. We're not chasing production growth for growth's sake—our Q1 2025 target is flat at 180-185 MBoepd—but prioritizing returns that compound shareholder value.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Thompson for an operational update.

Mike Thompson: Thank you, John. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 285 Mboe/d. We successfully brought the Mustang 12H-15H series online in the Permian, which is expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives.

Q3 was another strong quarter for Apex Energy, with our team executing flawlessly across our core acreage positions. We've continued to deliver industry-leading capital efficiency while de-risking our multi-year drilling inventory, all in a WTI environment averaging $82 per barrel—up 8% quarter-over-quarter—and Henry Hub gas holding steady around $2.75.

Starting with key well results, our flagship Permian Basin program continues to outperform. In the Delaware Basin, we brought online the Mustang 12H-15H series in Lea County, New Mexico—a six-well pad targeting the Second Bone Spring and Wolfcamp A/B benches. These Wolfcamp stack laterals averaged 12,500 feet, with proppant intensities north of 2,500 pounds per foot and 90-day IPs averaging 1,850 Boe/d, blending 72% oil. That's a 15% uplift over our Q2 Delaware averages, driven by our optimized completion designs incorporating dissolvable diverter balls and engineered fiber systems to enhance cluster efficiency—we're now seeing 95% cluster initiation rates based on fiber optic diagnostics. Estimated Ultimate Recovery, or EUR, on these wells is tracking at 1.4 MMBoe per well, with D&C costs at just $7.2 million per well, down 12% from last year thanks to our pad drilling efficiencies and supply chain optimizations with key partners like Halliburton and Liberty Energy.

Over in the Midland Basin, our Glasscock County pads—the Rattlesnake 4H-7H—delivered even stronger results in the Upper Spraberry. These 10,000-foot laterals posted 30-day IPs of 1,120 Boe/d, 68% oil, with EURs of 950 MBoe. Notably, our net pay thickness averaged 180 feet across the three-bench stack, with porosity exceeding 10% in the target intervals. These results validate our seismic reprocessing efforts using full-waveform inversion, which helped us high-grade locations away from parent-child interference zones. Overall Permian success rate year-to-date is 99%, with 42 gross wells turned-to-flow, adding 75,000 Boe/d to production—fully offsetting our 20% Q/Q decline curve through the quarter.

Shifting to the Eagle Ford, where we're focusing on our oil window in Karnes and DeWitt Counties, the Condor 3H-5H pad was a standout. These 14,000-foot laterals in the Lower Eagle Ford Shale targeted a 120-foot pay window with TOC over 4%. Initial production hit 2,100 Boe/d per well, 82% oil, with 60-day rates holding at 1,650 Boe/d—a 22% beat to our type curve. D&C costs here came in at $6.8 million, benefiting from our electric frac crews, which reduced emissions by 40% versus diesel and cut water sourcing costs via recycled produced water at 85% utilization. This ties into our ESG commitments; we're on track for Scope 1 methane intensity below 0.2% this year, ahead of peers like Pioneer and Occidental.

On the gas side, our Haynesville position in East Texas remains a bright spot amid softer nat gas prices. The Owl Creek 8H-10H wells in San Augustine County—our longest laterals yet at 15,200 feet—posted peak IPs of 18 MMcf/d, with 180-day EURs of 12 Bcf per well. Completion designs featured 3,000 lbs/ft proppant and 40 bpm stages, achieving fracture half-lengths of 450 feet per our DFIT analysis. These wells are flowing against 7,500 psi pressures, underscoring the high deliverability of our core acreage. We've hedged 70% of our 2024 Haynesville gas at $3.10/MMBtu strip, providing downside protection.

Internationally, our offshore Gulf of Mexico program advanced meaningfully. The Lucius North appraisal well, sidetracked from our 2022 discovery, encountered 150 feet of net oil pay in the Miocene sands, with porosities of 22% and Sw of 18%. Flow tests yielded 8,000 Bopd on a 48/64 choke—exceeding pre-drill estimates by 25%. This de-risks a 100 MMboe resource on our 30% WI block, adjacent to Chevron's Anchor development. We're partnering with Schlumberger on subsea tiebacks to accelerate first oil in 2026, with sanctioning planned for Q1.

Looking at trends, our drilling inventory now stands at 4.2 years in the Permian, 3.8 years in Eagle Ford, and 2.5 years in Haynesville, based on half-cycle returns exceeding 60% at $70 WTI. Cycle times are down to 190 days spud-to-sales in Permian pads, a 25% improvement Y/Y, thanks to our automated rig floor tech from Nabors and AI-driven bit selection via Patterns platform. We've also launched a pilot in the Delaware using plasma pulse technology from GoFrac to enhance frac conductivity—early data shows 10% uplift in propped conductivity.

On future plans, we're guiding to 28-32 gross Permian wells in Q4, maintaining our three-rig Midland and four-rig Delaware fleets. Eagle Ford activity steps up to eight wells with two new pads, and we'll spud our first Lucius South exploration well in December. Total E&D capex for 2024 is now $1.65 billion, up 5% at the midpoint, allocated 65% Permian, 20% Eagle Ford, 10% Haynesville/GOM, and 5% new ventures. This supports 8-10% production growth in 2025, with Permian delivering 85% of the incrementals.

We're prioritizing returns over growth—our long laterals and refrac opportunities yield IRR north of 80%—while monitoring OPEC+ cuts and potential U.S. permitting reforms. If WTI sustains $80+, we'll flex up 10% in activity; conversely, we have toggles to idle rigs below $65. This positions us for peer-leading FCF yields of 15-18% next year.

Now I will turn it over to Lisa Chen for an update on our exploration activities.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Mike. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Permian Delaware Basin and are planning to drill 20 exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Energy Capital Partners. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on the Permian well results and how they inform your inventory?

Alex Rivera: Good morning, John. Happy to elaborate. The Mustang and Rattlesnake pads exemplify our focus on stack-pay development with superior returns. Those 90-day IPs of 1,850 Boe/d in Delaware and strong Midland EURs confirm our type curves and de-risk further inventory. We're seeing consistent outperformance from completion tweaks, extending our Tier 1 locations well into the decade.

Operator: Our next question comes from Laura Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Laura Chen: Good morning. What are your expectations for capex flexibility in 2025 amid price volatility?

John Ramirez: Good morning, Laura. Our $2.6-2.8 billion guidance is flexible by design, with toggles to adjust rig count based on WTI thresholds. At $80+, we can add 10% activity for higher FCF; below $65, we idle rigs while maintaining breakeven FCF. This return-focused approach ensures resilience.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Patel: Could you please provide more color on cost reduction initiatives and their link to ESG?

Mike Thompson: Good morning, David. Our LOE down to $6.50/boe ties directly to water recycling at 85% and electric fracs cutting diesel 40%. These not only save $250 million annually but align with emissions targets, like methane below 0.2%, enhancing both margins and sustainability profile.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Kline with Tudor Pickering. Please go ahead.

Robert Kline: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

Lisa Chen: Good morning, Robert. The Lucius North success de-risks 100 MMboe in GoM, accelerating tie-backs for 2026 first oil. Combined with Permian seismic insights, it bolsters our 10+ year inventory, allowing us to allocate capex to highest-ROI prospects while maintaining domestic emphasis amid global opportunities like Alaska pilots.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.

aspect_summary.ESG initiatives: Progress on emissions r: In Q3 2024, Scope 1+2 GHG emissions reduced 18% YoY to 12.4M MT CO2e, 22% ahead of 2025 target of 15-20% reduction from 2020 baseline; intensity fell to 18 kg CO2e/boe from 22 kg YoY. Methane intensity down 28% to 0.25% (on track for <0.20% by 2025); flaring down 42% to 0.8%. Q4 guidance: further 5% cut; $600M ESG capex in 2025.
aspect_summary.Exploration & Drilling activity updates:: Key results: Permian Delaware Mustang pad (12,500 ft laterals) 90-day IP 1,850 Boe/d (72% oil, EUR 1.4 MMboe); Midland Rattlesnake 30-day IP 1,120 Boe/d (EUR 950 MBoe); Eagle Ford Condor (14k ft) IP 2,100 Boe/d (82% oil); Haynesville Owl Creek peak IP 18 MMcf/d (EUR 12 Bcf); GoM Lucius North appraisal flow-tested 8,000 Bopd. Future plans: Q4 28-32 Permian wells (3-rig Midland, 4-rig Delaware), 8 Eagle Ford wells, Lucius South spud; Permian seismic complete, 20 expl wells next year.
aspect_summary.Capital expenditure guidance: Future spe: 2025 capex $2.6-2.8B (down 5-7% from 2024 $2.9B midpoint), 80-82% upstream ($2.2-2.3B): Permian 70% ($1.8-1.9B, 85-90 wells, 60-75% IRR, sub-$40 half-cycle payback); Eagle Ford $350-400M (20-25 wells, 50-65% IRR); Appalachia $150-200M (>40% ROI). Targets >50% IRR at $60 WTI, 25-30% ROCE, FCF breakeven at $55 WTI.
aspect_summary.Production guidance: Next quarter and fu: Q4 2024: 440-460 Mboe/d (5-10% seq increase from Q3 420 Mboe/d), oil 280-295 Mbbl/d; FY2024: 425-435 Mboe/d (+8% YoY). FY2025: 455-475 Mboe/d (+7-12%), oil 62-65%. Upside from Permian D&C (70% growth, 3-mile laterals IP30 1,800 Boe/d, 25-30 Mboe/d Q4 adds), Eagle Ford, GoM Winterfell ramp (18 Mboe/d plateau); offsets base 22-25% decline, Q1 turnarounds. Risks: $5/bbl WTI drop, service inflation, takeaway constraints; 55% oil hedged at $72/bbl.
aspect_summary.EBITDA: YoY change and key drivers: Q3 adj EBITDA $2.8B, +28% YoY from $2.2B (TTM $10.7B +32%). Drivers: realized pricing (+$450M, $72.50/boe +22%, oil $71.80/bbl, gas $3.25/Mcfe); production (+$380M, 285 Mboe/d +14%, oil 210 Mbopd +18%); cost savings (+$250M, LOE $6.50/boe -17% YoY, total lifting $8.20/boe -12%).
